name: Browser Sessions through a whole deployment
admits automatic page references after delayed forms and document changes
evidence: Automatic page references after delayed forms or document changes remain flaky. A rejected synchronous title-refresh approach made five reads take 12.0–18.5 s in Target.getTargetInfo, compared with 0.136–0.200 ms without CDP calls. Preserve the unchanged Chromium <1,000 ms assertion.

Required design points:

- A document-bound acknowledgement carrying identity, full URL and title together;
  ledger generation guards and URL equality cannot attribute a title across CDP
  sessions. Define bootstrap, same-URL reload and BFCache incarnation semantics.
- Recovery driven by the existing catalog revision, surviving the Host's 100 ms
  coalescing and `D → null → D`; preserve draft/freeze/selection guards and avoid
  duplicate work. Do not rotate document identity to signal readiness.
- A per-page refresh lifecycle with registration/reconnection reconciliation,
  retained dirty state, supersession, bounded failure handling and explicit
  recovery triggers. Failed or never-settling work cannot block another page or
  teardown; never promote the old-title fallback into a new document.
- Screencast recovery and browser-view navigation acknowledgement use private
  document identity. Optional-field parsing alone does not establish semantic
  compatibility with the previous release.

Required acceptance, failing first:

- Gate sampling across same-URL reload, BFCache, redirects, fragments, bootstrap,
  popups, closure and reversed event delivery on separate CDP sessions.
- Cover empty/same titles, discovery disabled, failed/never-settling refreshes,
  recovery and exact target ownership/record incarnation.
- Exercise pending-to-ready through actual Host coalescing, catalog-revision
  recovery, all composer guards, screencast recovery and recent-site recording;
  include previous-release parsing and behavior.
- Require zero candidate-triggered CDP calls and repeatable sub-millisecond busy
  reads; preserve the unchanged Chromium `<1,000 ms`, paused/crashed-renderer and
  257-frame assertions.
- Deliberately replace the old synchronous-unnotified-title and read-time-sampling
  test contracts with gated background-publication safety checks. Keep the
  URL-ahead refusal and independent case-2 tests. Reuse one journey for each
  affected flow; run focused regression checks locally and retain repeatable
  qualification artifacts.

local-cover-invariants
evidence: Owner input reorders a person's local keystrokes, never loses them: in VM run 20261029T030730Z-d2ca0afa (direct AppKit owner-input), 3 of 2071 numbered tokens arrived reordered, e.g. '1038|1039|1040|' as '1038|039|11040|', right after an owner input dispatch, with no front app, pointer or Space change. A person key routed to the owner's target during the guarded dispatch reaches it late and is sent on after later keys went directly to the person's app; PersonKeyOrder orders only keys typed after a key is sent on. The log does not identify which restart stage stalled. Shutdown draining a live Run/event is a hypothesis; no evidence establishes a missed background wakeup, wall-clock deadline expiry or execution-lease race. Fixture containment then forcibly removes run databases (57P01 administrator termination), explaining the later connection errors.
